identification.name: C/SiC (Woven Carbon Fibre / SiC Matrix, CMC)
identification.common_form_notes: Produced as near-net-shape panels by chemical vapour infiltration (CVI) or polymer infiltration and pyrolysis (PIP) of woven carbon preforms. Machining requires diamond tooling and produces hazardous dust; use wet cutting and respiratory protection.
identification.notes: Two-dimensional woven carbon-fibre / SiC ceramic matrix composite (CMC), approximately 40 vol% carbon fibre infiltrated by chemical vapour infiltration (CVI). Properties are for the in-plane (warp/fill) directions of a balanced 2D weave; through-thickness properties are substantially lower. The SiC matrix provides significantly better oxidation resistance than C/C composites, but uncoated carbon fibres oxidise above ~450 °C in air — environmental barrier coatings (EBC) extend service temperature. In inert atmosphere or with EBC, service to ~1400 °C is possible. Fracture is pseudo-ductile: fibre pullout and crack deflection provide far higher toughness than monolithic SiC despite nominally brittle constituents. Properties vary greatly with fibre architecture, number of CVI infiltration cycles, and residual porosity; treat all values as order-of-magnitude references and consult manufacturer datasheets for specific grades. Carbon fibres provide electrical conductivity in-plane (not characterised here).

typical_usage: Thermal protection systems and hot structures for hypersonic vehicles and re-entry bodies; high-performance aerospace brake discs (where C/C is limited by oxidation); rocket nozzle throat inserts and extensions; gas turbine combustor liners and heat shields; satellite structures requiring extreme specific stiffness at elevated temperature.
